item.subject: Mathematics
item.stem:
In the picture there are a number of geometric shapes, like circles, squares, rectangles, and triangles. For example, the sun looks like a circle.

Draw lines to three other different objects in the picture and write what shapes they look like.

[Image: A house and yard scene with geometric objects]

descriptors: Any three of square, rectangle, triangle, trapezoid, diamond/rhombus, kite correctly identified
Any two of the above plus circle
Any two of the above correctly identified
Any one of the above plus circle
Incorrect (including crossed out/erased, stray marks, illegible or off task)

item.figure_description:
A line drawing of a scene containing geometric elements:
- In the upper right sky, a circular shape is labeled "sun" with a line drawn to the label "circle".
- Behind the house are trees rendered with leafy texture.
- In the center is a two-story house:
  - The roof features two dormers, each topped with a triangular roof and containing a rectangular window divided into four square panes.
  - A small chimney is on the roof ridge.
  - The main facade is rectangular, featuring two rectangular windows (each divided into four panes) and a central rectangular front door.
  - The door contains a diamond-shaped (rhombus) window and a small round doorknob.
- In front of the door is a stone path composed of trapezoidal and triangular paving stones.
- To the lower left of the house stands a lamppost consisting of a circular light mounted on a tall, narrow rectangular post set in grass.
item.calibration: Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 1995 and 2003 fourth-grade mathematics data.

reference_items.subject: Mathematics
reference_items.stem:
Get to 20 Number Game

Two children, Joan and Herbert, are learning to play a game “Get to 20.” Here are the rules for the game.

GET TO 20
RULES

Pick Tiles: Each player draws three number tiles.

Add Tiles: Each player places the three tiles to make an addition problem with the sum total closest to 20.

For example, here are four ways a player who draws [1] , [4] , and [5] could place the tiles:

  [5] [1]          [4] [5]          [1] [5]             [1]
+     [4]    or  +     [1]    or  +     [4]    or     + [5]
---------        ---------        ---------         + [4]
       55               46               19         -----
                                                       10

This player should choose to show the addition problem
  15
+  4
----
  19
because 19 is the total closest to 20.

Joan and Herbert played the game “Get to 20.”

Joan picked [2] , [7] , and [9] . Herbert picked [1] , [3] , and [6] .

C. Herbert said, “If I pick [1] , [4] , and [6] , I can make 20 two different ways.”

Show two ways Herbert could make 20 with [1] , [4] , and [6] .

First way:

Second way:

Only one way correct 16 + 4 OR 14 + 6

slope.instructions: TIMSS scaled this 2-point item with the generalized partial credit model (GPCM), which TIMSS uses for constructed-response items worth 2 or 3 points, in the calibration "Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 1995 and 2003 fourth-grade mathematics data". What is the item's slope (discrimination) parameter a? A higher a means that the item separates students of lower and higher mathematics ability more sharply. Choose the value closest to it. The state also lists reference items: the calibrated TIMSS items of the same grade most similar to this one (never the item itself or its other parts), most similar first, with their percent correct and their calibrated parameters, each on the scale of its own calibration. Use them to place this item.

location.instructions: TIMSS scaled this 2-point item with the generalized partial credit model (GPCM), which TIMSS uses for constructed-response items worth 2 or 3 points, in the calibration "Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 1995 and 2003 fourth-grade mathematics data". What is the item's location (difficulty) parameter b? b is on a logit scale on which the students of the calibration average about 0; a higher b means a harder item. Choose the value closest to it. The state also lists reference items: the calibrated TIMSS items of the same grade most similar to this one (never the item itself or its other parts), most similar first, with their percent correct and their calibrated parameters, each on the scale of its own calibration. Use them to place this item.

step1.instructions: TIMSS scaled this 2-point item with the generalized partial credit model (GPCM), which TIMSS uses for constructed-response items worth 2 or 3 points, in the calibration "Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 1995 and 2003 fourth-grade mathematics data". What is the item's step 1 parameter d1? In the GPCM, b - d1 is the ability at which earning the first point becomes more likely than earning no point, so a higher d1 means that this point is earned at a lower ability; the steps sum to 0. Choose the value closest to it. The state also lists reference items: the calibrated TIMSS items of the same grade most similar to this one (never the item itself or its other parts), most similar first, with their percent correct and their calibrated parameters, each on the scale of its own calibration. Use them to place this item.
